rationale: UPHELD on the inspected original, subject to the qualifications stated here. Verified both card file hashes and source PDF SHA256 3bce4d490526a69516217faf43b66b62adf565a388b622f6d1e9225faffdcdf5. Independently rendered and visually read PDF pp. 622-623, printed pp. 1393-1394. EO 5989 begins below the completed EO 5988 and ends at [No. 5989] before EO 5990. The operative text identifies Dr. Charles Orrin Townsend, Chief of the Sugar Division of the United States Tariff Commission, and ends: 'is hereby exempted from the provisions of that section until January 31, 1934.' Thus 1934-01-31 is the express terminal date of the one personal section 204 retirement exemption. The complete sentence has no earlier terminating event, independent appointment, payment, reporting, delegated authority, or recurring command; the act title, fiscal-year date, statutory authority and employment description are predicates, not additional operative obligations. No express savings or prospective residual appears; accrued service or pay would be historical consequences rather than continuation of the exemption. The cited substantive quotation matches the image, allowing OCR whitespace and line-break differences. Material qualification: the original alone does not prove the absence of an intervening revocation, extension, earlier death or separation. I did not independently rerun the reported later-source searches; their coverage limits, especially pre-1937 coverage, remain. 'Until January 31' does not by itself settle inclusive versus exclusive time of day, which the card expressly discloses. I uphold the date and bounded whole-case conclusion as qualified, not a claim that the image establishes exact time of termination or exhaustively excludes external earlier events.

REJECTED. Verified both card file hashes and source PDF SHA256 3bce4d490526a69516217faf43b66b62adf565a388b622f6d1e9225faffdcdf5. Independently rendered and visually read PDF p. 45, printed p. 816, including EO 5595 from its heading through signature/date and [No. 5595]. The operative sentence orders that flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and Ohio 'be placed at half mast to-day and on the day of the funeral service at Cincinnati, Ohio, Saturday, April 11, 1931.' The signing date is April 9, 1931. The conjunction 'and on' makes April 11 an operative second scheduled occasion; it is not merely explanatory context. Consequently April 9 placement cannot fulfill the complete command, and the claimed 1931-04-10 first_end/whole_order_end truncates the order while the April 11 duty remains prospective. The substantive source quote itself accurately preserves the decisive words and contradicts the judgment_reason and research_rationale. If an exclusive next-day representation is used, the ordinary completion boundary would be April 12 after the April 11 occasion, rather than April 10; the original does not specify an exact hour. The whole order contains this single flag command with two required occasions, no other independent power or recurring command, and no express savings, payment rights or continuing residual. No earlier terminating event appears in the original. I did not independently rerun reported later-source searches and cannot exclude an external intervening instrument or establish actual performance from this page alone. Those uncertainties do not cure the explicit omission of the April 11 command, so the whole-case claim is rejected even though eventual termination is consistent with the source.
